commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

content.text:
The Spec tab's Analysis group now has a "View Divergence Reports" button after Analyze Divergence. It opens the Divergence panel on the latest saved report without starting an analysis, and earlier reports open from "Saved reports" on the Report tab. Tests pass (161, 1 ignored); I haven't tried it in the running app.

**One behaviour change:** Analyze Divergence now always starts a fresh analysis. Before, it showed the latest saved report when there was one; that's now the new button's job.

**How the two buttons behave:**
- **View Divergence Reports:** it has a document icon and is disabled until a project is open. It isn't primary, so it doesn't show in the collapsed ribbon; Analyze Divergence still does.
- **No reports yet:** viewing shows "No divergence reports yet", a line saying an analysis is saved once it's over, and an "Analyze" button.
- **A minimized panel:** both buttons bring it back rather than opening a second one. View Divergence Reports shows the latest report, and Analyze Divergence starts an analysis. If one is already running, neither interrupts it.
- **The activity list:** clicking a running analysis there still just brings the panel back.

**Code:**
- `src/divergence_view.rs`: an `Opening` setting (analyze or view reports), a `ViewDivergenceReports` action, and the empty state.
- `src/main_window.rs`: `open_divergence` takes the opening mode.
- `src/ribbon/spec_tab.rs` and `src/ribbon/mod.rs`: the new button and command.

**Tests:**
- A new test opens the panel to view reports with none saved. It checks no agent runs and the empty state shows. It then clicks Analyze and checks a report is saved. Finally it brings the panel back both ways: viewing starts nothing, analyzing starts a new run.
- The saved-reports test now opens its second panel to view reports.
- The ribbon test checks that Build, Analyze Divergence and View Divergence Reports sit in that order.

**Spec:**
- `spec/ui/components/ribbon/spec-tab/index.pi`: the Analysis group and the new command.
- `spec/scope/divergence/index.pi`: the two ways of opening the panel, the empty state, and what each button does to a minimized panel.
- `spec/scope/application/MainWindow.pi`: the new command.

`piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` all ran cleanly, and the app builds with no warnings.
